question_text: The Congress passes a law that imposes a tax on religious organizations for their income from commercial activities. A religious group challenges the law as unconstitutional. Under Article VIII of the 1987 Constitution, what power does the Supreme Court have to review this law?

options.text: The Supreme Court can declare the law unconstitutional if it finds that it violates the Constitution, through its power of judicial review.
The Supreme Court can only review the law if the President requests an advisory opinion.
The Supreme Court cannot review the law because it involves taxation, which is a political question.
The Supreme Court can review the law but only if it is challenged by at least one-third of the members of Congress.
